subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Gift Exchange in Labor
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gift Exchange in Labor.

hook.text: A firm pays above minimum wage. Workers are not contractually obligated to work harder. Yet productivity rises 20%. Why?

buildup.text: The gift exchange model: employers offer generous wages as a gift, and employees reciprocate with higher effort.

discovery.text: Akerlof proposed efficiency wages: above-market pay buys loyalty and effort that monitoring alone can't achieve.

twist.text: The gift must feel intentional. Mandated minimum wage increases don't produce the same reciprocity as voluntary.

climax.text: Reciprocity works in both directions. Pay cuts trigger effort reduction disproportionate to the cut.

punchline.text: Pay generously and they work harder. Cut pay and they work less.

quiz.question: Why does above-market pay increase worker effort?
options: Workers fear being fired if they do not reciprocate
Workers feel the generous wage is a gift and reciprocate with effort
It is legally required to work harder when paid more

details.summary: Gift exchange in labor markets describes the reciprocal relationship where employers pay above-market wages as a gift, and employees reciprocate with above-minimum effort, creating a cooperative equilibrium that standard economic theory cannot explain.
details.whyItMatters: Gift exchange explains why firms pay efficiency wages above market clearing levels and why workers voluntarily contribute effort beyond what monitoring requires. This reciprocity fundamentally shapes employment relationships.
takeaways: Higher-than-required wages elicit higher-than-required effort from workers
Reciprocity creates stable above-equilibrium wages and productivity
Standard economic theory predicts minimum wages and minimum effort

faq.question: Why do firms pay more than the minimum necessary wage?
faq.answer: Laboratory and field experiments show that above-market wages trigger reciprocal effort increases that more than offset the higher cost. Workers feel grateful for generous pay and work harder in return, raising productivity and profits.

faq.question: Does gift exchange work equally across all cultures?
faq.answer: The strength varies. Cultures with stronger reciprocity norms show larger gift exchange effects. In highly individualistic settings or where monitoring is strict, the effect weakens because effort is driven by surveillance rather than gratitude.
